mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.stated_objective_pain_point: High failure rates and intuition-based design in university-class CubeSats motivate rigorous systems engineering and a reusable CRM for instruction and mission-specific design/build.

mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.system_boundary_level_of_abstraction: Generic CubeSat mission enterprise with space and ground segments, generic/loose subsystem definitions, representative subsystem components, external environment/constraints, provided services, and mission-specific tailoring to physical architecture. The CRM deliberately avoids imposing implementation constraints.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.minimal_or_excluded_modeling: The CRM is methodology-agnostic and provides a library rather than prescribing all model elements/relationships. mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.required_prior_behavioral_domain_knowled: The mission team chooses Fundamental, Representative, or Detailed package levels depending on experience with space-ground systems, MBSE, and SysML; the paper assumes access to a graphical SysML tool and some systems engineering/modeling competence.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.handling_limited_behavioral_knowledge: Generic and loosely defined subsystems, use-case narratives, representative components, table-based population, and reference information allow teams to incrementally add mission-specific behavior and physical components.

generality_reuse_mechanism_v1_1_reasonin.rationale: The paper explicitly presents the CRM as a reusable CubeSat community starting point and OMG specification candidate, not just a high-level one-off model. Reuse is supported by a template/reference model, model-element library, stereotypes/profiles, generic logical architecture, loose subsystem definitions, table-based population workflow, and user guidance. Do not add interface-focused model or specific-mission model with reusable method only.

evidence.quote: Because the initial model was RAX-centric and not suitable for reuse... Develop a CubeSat Reference Model (CRM) that a CubeSat team can use as a starting point for its mission
The CRM provides a library of model elements but does not dictate what model elements and relationships to use.
The CRM provides a CubeSat logical architecture. The logical components are abstractions of the physical components... without imposing implementation constraints.
The CubeSat and Ground subsystems are generically and loosely defined as a starting point for the mission-specific CubeSat team.
It is a template model that provides building blocks that can be specialized to support MBSE CubeSat design.
A use case can be described in a Use Case Description document... and then, if warranted, detailed in a SysML model.

RQ1: Provides a reusable SysML CubeSat Reference Model with generic mission/system/subsystem/ground packages, requirements, use cases, technical measures, and validation strategy.
Explicitly addresses minimal/generic modeling by using loosely defined subsystems and allowing mission-specific tailoring rather than dictating relationships.
RQ2: Claims system-level reuse, traceability, reproducibility, interoperability, stakeholder communication, and decision support, but evidence is mainly artifact description and plans.
No EPS-specific reliability/reproducibility/integrability outcomes are demonstrated; prior RAX power trade studies are lineage evidence only.
RQ3: Reports generic verify/satisfy properties and parametric technical-measure analysis that could support pre-physical checks.
Does not present an EPS verification-procedure model, EPS test cases/procedures, or SIL/HIL/automated verification artifacts.
